sources.entry: Music Router - Stops Music.app from auto-launching and routes media keys to the app you're actually using. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/drumandbytes/music-router) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A macOS menu-bar utility that stops Music.app/iTunes from launching and routes media keys to the player you actually want.
summary.what_it_does: Music Router runs in the macOS menu bar and quits Music.app or iTunes when it launches, so it does not open unexpectedly. Media keys are intercepted before macOS launches Music; other launch triggers such as AirPlay, Handoff or Siri are closed right after they start. If an app or browser tab already owns Now Playing, the media key goes to it unchanged. When nothing is playing, it resumes the last scriptable player or starts a replacement app (Spotify, TIDAL, VLC, a web player, or any app) and actually plays it. You can pin a media-key target among several players from the menu or with a remappable global shortcut (⌃⌥⌘M by default). It includes a fallback CoreAudio check when Now Playing detection fails, plus a Settings window, launch at login, permission reset and opt-in debug logging, and a bundled musicrouter-media command-line tool for scripts.
use_cases: send media keys to Spotify or VLC instead of Apple Music
prevent iTunes launching when pressing play
stop AirPlay or Siri from opening Music
resume the last music player with the keyboard
script media control from a status bar
notable: Intercepts media keys before macOS launches Music, so there is no launch-then-quit flash
Lets whatever is already playing keep the media keys
Replacement app is started and actually played, not just opened
Bundled MediaRemote adapter and musicrouter-media command-line tool, no extra install
Remappable global shortcut to cycle the media-key target
caveats: Music launched by AirPlay, Handoff or Siri is closed after it starts, not prevented
Now Playing detection uses a private framework and may break on macOS updates; a fallback keeps blocking and routing working
Requires Input Monitoring and Accessibility permissions (Device Control and Data Access on macOS 27)
Ad-hoc signed, so macOS shows an unidentified developer prompt on first launch
